subject.title: feat(browser): pair the Chrome extension directly to a remote gateway

question: Should OpenClaw accept a direct Chrome extension-to-Gateway WebSocket route guarded by the host-local relay secret in the URL query, or keep the cross-machine relay behind authenticated node-host or tunnel topology?
rationale: This changes the trust boundary for signed-in browser sessions; code review can identify the lazy-start bug, but cannot decide the permanent security and product boundary.

options.title: Accept direct route with guardrails
options.body: Require the lazy-start fix, inspectable live proof, TLS/query-token documentation, and explicit security sign-off before merging the direct route.

options.title: Keep node-host or tunnel only
options.body: Reject the public direct route and continue solving the cross-machine case through an authenticated browser-node or tunnel topology.

options.title: Pause for browser API design
options.body: Hold this PR until the broader browser-backend/plugin API strategy for https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/53599 is settled.

recommendation.title: Accept direct route with guardrails
recommendation.body: Require the lazy-start fix, inspectable live proof, TLS/query-token documentation, and explicit security sign-off before merging the direct route.

likelyOwner.reason: This account owns the recent extension relay implementation and is the clearest routing owner for the direct-Gateway follow-up.
